 KCAU Sioux City Follow How LIHEAP can help Siouxlanders with heating costs
 Nik Wilson Thu, November 12, 2026 at 8:19 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. SIOUX CITY , Iowa ( KCAU ) — As temperatures in Siouxland drop, heating costs will rise. That's where some financial assistance can come in handy.
 The Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program , also known as LIHEAP, is a federally funded program. That's designed to help qualifying low-income households pay for a portion of their heating costs.
 Jean Logan with the Community Action Agency of Siouxland told us while the program has a lot of requirements, there is some flexibility.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "So, we can look at last year's tax returns or we can look at the last 30 days of income," Logan said. "That would be to accommodate people that maybe had a recent job loss or an illness and their income might've changed in the past 30 days."

 The annual application period in Iowa runs from November 1st to April 30th. In order to qualify, your household income must be 200 percent or lower than the federal poverty level.
 Advertisement Advertisement Logan told us the most amount of money an applicant could receive is $800. So far, the Community Action Agency of Siouxland has received 1,126 applications and they have approved 1,035.
